newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee edges higher, rumours abound.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee edges higher, rumours abound.

text.p: Indonesian coffee prices were higher on Monday despite steady declines in London values, as rumours of wash-outs and contract renegotiations swept the market amid tight supply, traders said.

"There has been market talk of wash-outs involving some foreign buyers," one senior trader said. "There is talk of payments of $100-$150 a tonne for the washed-out contracts, but of course no one has owned up yet."
Another trader said there have been rumours of contracts being renegotiated between sellers and exporters because the deals were done when prices were much lower.
"There's not much beans in the market but there are plenty of rumours," the trader said.
"But what is more or less certain is that there have been some rollover of positions from July to September because the sellers were not able to fix prices for the July contracts."
He said the rollover was due to sellers finding the July price not to their liking, and would rather pay the price difference between the September and July contracts.

The traders said London's September robusta contract was expected to open $10-$20 higher later on Monday. The contract ended $4 higher at $1,775 a tonne on Friday, while July fell $16 to close at $1,740.

They said grade four robusta was quoted at 4,000-4,100 rupiah per kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, unchanged from a week ago. The export price was quoted at $1,650-$1,700 a tonne, against $1,600-$1,650. The said some sellers were quoting as high as $1,750 a tonne.
"Those on the high side are essentially fishing," one trader said. "They are trying to show that local supply is very tight. But buyers will not been keen at those levels."
Another trader said some exporters were continuing to buy beans to fill contracts, but added that others were mostly sidelined because of the high values.
